children: Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) delivered a blowout fiscal Q3 with strong revenue, cash flow and net income driven by AI infrastructure demand, even as shares fell on U.S. reports easing memory sourcing rules; analysts remain bullish while Micron pivots HBM priorities to compete with Samsung and SK Hynix.
Micron Technology, Inc. Revenue Growth, AI Demand
: Micron (MU) posted fiscal Q3 revenue $41.46B, up sharply QoQ and YoY; operating cash flow $25.39B and GAAP net income $28.24B. Company cites AI infrastructure demand.
Micron Technology, Inc. U.S. DRAM/NAND Uncertainty
: Micron (MU) sank after reports the U.S. may allow Apple to buy DRAM from CXMT and NAND from YMTC. Analysts cite CXMT scale/yield limits; policy comments and lobbying added uncertainty.
Micron Technology, Inc. Maintains Buy Stance
: UBS and Bank of America kept Buy on Micron (MU) after meetings on supply deals and margins; both cited durable earnings. UBS PT $1,625, BofA PT $1,550.
Micron Technology, Inc. Prioritizes HBM AI
: Micron (MU) said at Hot Chips it’s prioritizing HBM for AI, citing cooling and advanced packaging challenges, and stressing the need to keep pace with Samsung and SK Hynix.
